previous_statement: Conditional composition step. Assume epsilon<=e_0/2 and rho<=a_merge=e_0/2. Then e=rho+epsilon<=e_0. Once nodes 1.1.1, 1.1.2, 1.2, and 1.3 are validated, mu_1, Gamma_1, and alpha_1 are linear bijections, gamma=alpha_1 Gamma_1 mu_1 is bijective, gamma_n=I_n tensor gamma, and every gamma_n has the homomorphism and two-sided norm bounds with constant C_merge=max{K_hom,K_norm,3}; this is exactly an extended C_merge*e-isomorphism. This conclusion is expressly conditional on the added epsilon bound and therefore does not establish the current root contract.
new_statement: Second obstruction: exact involution preservation. Even after adding epsilon<=e_0/2 and rho<=a_merge=e_0/2, and even conditionally assuming nodes 1.1.1, 1.1.2, 1.2, and 1.3 validated, the factorization establishes that gamma is bijective, gamma_n=I_n tensor gamma, and the amplifications have the asserted approximate unit, multiplication, involution, and two-sided norm bounds. But the allowed source definition of a delta-homomorphism in the *-algebra setting additionally requires the exact identity gamma_n(X^dagger)=gamma_n(X)^dagger. Node 1.2 supplies only ||gamma_n(X^dagger)-gamma_n(X)^dagger||<=K_hom*e*||X||, which does not imply that identity for e>0, regardless of the choice of C_merge. Therefore the amplifications have not been shown to be C_merge*e-homomorphisms, so def-extended-delta-inclusion does not yield an extended C_merge*e-isomorphism. Thus the conditional theorem in node 1.4.1 also requires exact involution compatibility (or a changed target definition), in addition to the missing epsilon-smallness hypothesis; under the allowed inputs, this is an obstruction rather than a proof of the root contract.
